name: Engine R4: runtime on one WebGLRenderer, MotionPlayer, lab page and e2e
description: Wires schema, textures, 2D nodes, three layers, effects (isolated, three, stage), presets and tweens into MotionRuntime on a single Three WebGLRenderer, wraps it in <MotionPlayer>, adds /motion-lab.html and a Playwright spec (npm run engine:e2e) that checks every fixture for readiness, determinism, motion, colour and transparency. No Pixi.

userStories.title: assemble(): stage, nodes, isolation, presets and tweens on one clock
userStories.description: As an engine developer, I want the whole build pipeline in one function that runs without WebGL so that wiring bugs are caught by unit tests.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section 'assemble' (steps 1 to 7).

Create engine/src/runtime/assemble.ts implementing steps 1 to 7: stage Scene and createStageCamera, nodes via createNode with factories.three, displays added in order, renderOrder by depth-first index on every mesh, isolateNode for 2D nodes with enabled effects, validateTargets warnings, MotionClock, expandPresets plus layer tweens compiled with a resolve that sends effect:<id> to the isolation or the three node and everything else to node.resolveTarget, buildStageChain, primeTimeline.
Return { stage, camera, nodes, clock, renderAt, warnings, destroy } (renderAt is completed in US-002; for now it may only set visibility).
Create engine/src/runtime/assemble.test.ts with renderer null, the chain test factory, a shapes-only doc and a doc with a fake three factory.
acceptanceCriteria: assemble on a doc with two shapes and a group with one child returns 4 nodes, the stage has 3 children in layer order, and the second shape's meshes have a higher renderOrder than the first's
A shape with enter fadeIn has node.alpha.value 0 at its start and its base alpha after the preset duration (via clock.seek)
A text or shape layer with a glow effect is isolated (its display contains a plane, not its content), and a tween on effect:g reaches the fake chain's ref
A tween with an unknown property becomes one warning containing the layer id; destroy() destroys every node and the clock (spied)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: renderAt(t): visibility, opacity, node and isolation updates, stage render
userStories.description: As an engine developer, I want each clock update to show exactly the layers that are on, fade groups correctly and render once so that every frame is a function of time.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md (renderAt) and engine/src/stage2d/opacity.ts.

Complete renderAt(t): display.visible = isVisible for every node; applyOpacityTree on the root nodes; for visible nodes node.update?.(t, frame) and the isolation's update; then stageChain ? stageChain.render(renderer) : renderer.render(stage, camera); skip rendering when renderer is null.
Add tests to assemble.test.ts with a fake renderer object (render and setRenderTarget spies) passed as renderer and the chain test factory.
acceptanceCriteria: A layer from 1 to 2 is invisible at seek 0.5, visible at 1.5 and invisible at 2
A fake three node from 0 to 3 gets update(1, 30) on seek(1) and no update on seek(4)
Each seek renders exactly once: renderer.render is called once per seek when there are no stage effects, and the stage chain's render once when there are
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: MotionRuntime: WebGLRenderer, load, play, seek, whenReady, renderFrame, readPixel
userStories.description: As a page author, I want one object that owns the canvas and the renderer and plays a doc so that pages and the player component stay thin.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md section 'MotionRuntime' (renderer settings, load steps, whenReady, destroy).

Create engine/src/runtime/MotionRuntime.ts as specified, with the WebGLRenderer created through an injectable factory (for tests) and the settings from the doc; load parses, keeps the previous doc on failure, destroys the previous assembly, loads textures and three assets, assembles; readPixel reads the canvas (WebGL readPixels with y flipped to doc coordinates).
Create engine/src/runtime/index.ts and engine/src/runtime/MotionRuntime.test.ts with a fake renderer factory.
acceptanceCriteria: load of an invalid doc returns ok false with errors and keeps the previous clock
whenReady(0.05) resolves false when a node's ready never settles and true when all settle (fake timers)
The renderer is created with preserveDrawingBuffer true, pixel ratio 1, outputColorSpace SRGBColorSpace and toneMapping NoToneMapping (checked on the fake)
destroy() disposes the assembly and calls renderer.dispose() and forceContextLoss()
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.description: As a React author, I want a drop-in player with controls and a handle like the director's PlayerHandle so that a later swap is mechanical.

metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; browser checks load assets from web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/README.md and the spec doc the story names before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.

Porting is allowed: read tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src (a read-only copy of the library, inside this repo) and copy what engine/docs/port-map.md says. Never edit anything under tmp/. Every ported file starts with `// Ported from reacthub-pixitweenjs <path> (MIT).` and is cleaned up to strict TypeScript.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore` under engine/. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.

engine/ is Three.js + GSAP only: it must not import from web/, server/, shared/, `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `pixi.js`, `pixi-filters`, `@pixi/*` or `@react-three/*`. Only the web stub files listed in metadata.sharedEdits may import engine/.

Do not touch the director app: nothing under server/, shared/, web/src/ (except the stub files under web/ listed in metadata.sharedEdits) or the existing e2e/ specs. Config files only as listed in metadata.sharedEdits.
Everything you build goes under engine/ (src/, fixtures/, lab/, e2e/, docs/). Edit only the files named in the story's steps and their tests, plus the small edits listed in metadata.sharedEdits.

Determinism: no Math.random, Date.now or performance.now in anything that affects pixels; no GSAP `overwrite`, no `immediateRender: true`, no infinite `repeat` (engine/docs/02-timeline.md, determinism rules).
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic and object construction; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.
Do not add a dependency the spec does not name (`postprocessing` and `@types/three` are already declared).

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/engine/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server the owner runs on http://localhost:5173 (do not start another on a different port); if it is not running, run `npm run engine:e2e` instead.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.
Three.js only: no import of pixi.js, pixi-filters, @pixi/* or @react-three/* (lint enforces it).
The package.json edit is limited to making sure the script "engine:e2e": "playwright test -c engine/playwright.config.ts" exists.
